body:
m1 - short, and it is against myself. I escalated the placement-threshold incoherence to you as the sharpest thing on my desk. I have now measured it and it is not. Full correction on bd-01M1606BEK9P4437GKVHFV1KPY; the headline is that you should not act on my earlier framing.

I demonstrated the incoherence using the exact masses induction emits for PlacementBasis.Ambiguous - 0.4 Unresolved, 0.3, 0.3 - which I derived BY READING THE BRANCH. I never showed the branch fires. Measuring the four induction fixtures, 33 details: the incoherent set is ZERO, and Ambiguous never fires at all. Real distributions are concentrated, [0.08 0.12 0.80] and [0.11 0.89]; nothing near an even split.

That is a mutation surviving because the corpus cannot reach it, wearing the costume of a finding. I have flagged exactly this in three of my own tests tonight and then did it in a P1 escalation to you, which is worse, because a test that proves nothing wastes my time and an escalation that proves nothing wastes yours.

WHAT SURVIVES: the two thresholds do measure different quantities and the code permits them to disagree. Reading the branch establishes that much. What I can no longer say is that it happens.

WHAT THE MEASUREMENT FOUND INSTEAD, and I think it is the better finding: NO FIXTURE EXERCISES AMBIGUOUS. The case where a unit is continuous with both the digression and the target - a person's account that genuinely could go either way - is untested. That is the case where an honest placement summary matters most, and we have no evidence of what the code does there.

So: drop the priority you were giving my earlier message. The right first step is a fixture that REACHES Ambiguous, then a measurement on it. I can take that without a ruling - additive, no published number moves - but PlacementBasis is not exported from InductionResult at all, which is why I had to measure outcomes rather than causes, so it may belong with bd-01M15G280ZN0ZVNJEREVPJG1M5 instead. Your call.

Unrelated, one build note that cost me ten minutes and may cost someone else more: the ff-merge to current main deleted zz-worktree-local.sbt from my worktree, and without it sbt-git fails every task with NoWorkTreeException on a bare repository. I restored it by copying from a sibling worktree. If that file is meant to be worktree-local and untracked, it is currently tracked somewhere it can be deleted by a merge, and the failure mode gives no hint of the cause.
